summary: brief.md synthesizes 26 freshly found sources across all 8 research steps and meets the plan's success bar on each of identify / reach / pitch with at least one concrete, checkable tactic beyond the two prior runs: identify (ChurchStaffing.com and ZipRecruiter job-board feeds naming real churches staffing paid small-group roles, plus a ChurchLeaders-documented title-variant search set), reach (faith.tools free submission and paid sponsorship path; Small Group Network ALIGN/ACCELERATE with attendee pricing of $124-$209 and a $49/month subscription; RightNow Media's 30,000+ church / 4M+ user base and monthly leader email; Mark Howell as a named practitioner intermediary), and pitch (SmartGroups' free-single-group tier as the one documented offer structure; four objection categories each backed by at least one source, three by non-vendor sources). The ministry-coordinator question is closed with three corroborating sources (UMC, CRC, ChurchStaffing) confirming the role implements rather than decides. Overall reliability is moderate: identification and conference-pricing claims rest on primary/checkable sources; scale figures are vendor self-reported; the tool-fragmentation objection is single-vendor-sourced; all outreach-script and pitch-language material is cross-domain EdTech and labeled as such; Step 2 (online communities) is effectively unevaluated because no size/activity data was retrievable. The brief includes a validated Mermaid hierarchy diagram of decision vs. implementation roles, flags a correction to the plan (LifeGroups.com is Life.Church's internal brand, not a network), lists the gathering agent's five round-cap gaps, and poses nine open questions for the critiquing stage, most importantly whether the job-board mechanic reaches small/independent churches and whether the EdTech champion analog survives the volunteer-vs-paid-professional difference.
